title: Carthage's Tophet: Burial Ground or Place of Sacrifice?

scenes.name: 1a Cold open: 1921
scenes.heading: Someone was digging up carved stones by moonlight.

scenes.name: 1b Urns
scenes.text: Urn after urn of burnt bones: of infants, and of young lambs.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 1c Two teams
scenes.text: Two teams. The same remains. Conflicting conclusions.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 1d The question
scenes.text: Offered to the gods, or mourned?
scenes.label: open-question

scenes.name: 1e Title
scenes.heading: Carthage's Tophet: Burial Ground or Place of Sacrifice?

scenes.name: 2a From Tyre to Carthage
scenes.title: A Phoenician city, linked to Tyre

events.label: Founded on the Gulf of Tunis
A trading power across the Mediterranean

scenes.name: 2d The tophet
scenes.text: Archaeologists call it the tophet.
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: The Hebrew Bible uses the same word, Topheth, for a condemned place near Jerusalem

scenes.name: 3b One season
scenes.label: urns lifted in a single season, 1925
scenes.sourceNote: Kelsey expedition · as described by Stager 2014

events.label: Stelae spotted being dug up at night
Kelsey expedition: about 1,000 urns in one season

scenes.name: 3c Six centuries
scenes.text: Hundreds of urns, buried over some six centuries
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: c. 8th century BC – 146 BC (excavators' dating) · trench of roughly 150 m²

scenes.name: 3d Contents
scenes.text: Infants. Young lambs. Sometimes both, in one urn.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 3e Amulets
scenes.label: of urns studied held amulets: only ever with human remains

scenes.name: 4a Diodorus
scenes.author: Diodorus Siculus
scenes.text: Claims that during a siege in 310 BC the Carthaginians sacrificed 200 children of noble families to the god he calls Cronus.
scenes.gap: Written about 250 years after the events

scenes.name: 4b Plutarch
scenes.author: Plutarch
scenes.text: Describes parents offering their own children, and mothers forbidden to weep.

scenes.name: 4c Outsiders
scenes.text: The accusers were outsiders: Greek authors, not Carthaginians.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 4d Supposed eye-witnesses
scenes.text: "Supposed eye-witness reports"
scenes.label: interpretation

scenes.name: 4e Not proof
scenes.text: Hostile sources are not necessarily false. On their own, they are not proof.

scenes.name: 5a Voices in stone
scenes.caption: A stela from the Carthage tophet, 3rd century BC. Its inscription is not translated here.
scenes.credit: Photo: Rama · CC BY-SA 2.0 FR · Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon

scenes.name: 5b The vow formula
scenes.text: "…because he heard his voice and blessed him"
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: Typical vow formula on tophet stelae · translation: Stager 2014

scenes.name: 5c Promised gifts
scenes.text: Promised gifts, given after a prayer was answered
scenes.label: interpretation

scenes.name: 5d mlk
scenes.text: mlk: a kind of sacrificial offering, not a god called "Moloch"
scenes.label: interpretation

scenes.name: 5e The priest stela
scenes.text: A priest holding an infant: alive, or already dead?
scenes.label: interpretation
scenes.attribution: Stager 2014 (living child) vs Schwartz et al. 2017 (deceased infant)

scenes.name: 6a Age is the key
scenes.text: The case rests largely on age at death
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: Estimated from small, fire-damaged fragments of skull, hip and teeth

scenes.name: 6b Neonatal line
scenes.caption: The neonatal line forms only if a baby survives at least a week or two after birth.

scenes.name: 6c Shrinkage
scenes.caption: Fire shrinks bone. Schwartz et al. tested corrections of up to 25%.

scenes.name: 6d Correction matters
scenes.text: How much you correct for that changes the answer.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 7a Two verdicts
scenes.title: Same bones, two verdicts

left.heading: Many died before or around birth
points: 2017: 24% prenatal, 15% around birth, 17% under one month
Fits natural infant mortality; occasional sacrifice not ruled out

right.heading: Most died at 1–1.5 months
points: Argue cremation can erase the neonatal line
Unlike an ordinary infant cemetery: sacrifice "very probable"

scenes.footer: Each team argued in print that the other had erred (2010–2017).

scenes.name: 7b Same bones
scenes.text: Same bones. Two verdicts.
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: Published exchange in PLoS ONE and Antiquity, 2010–2017

scenes.name: 8a Beyond Carthage
scenes.title: Tophets: central Mediterranean (so far)
scenes.note: Selected sites · Zita: later, comparative evidence

scenes.name: 8b Zita
scenes.text: Zita: hard lives, careful burial, no concrete sign of sacrifice
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: Cerezo-Román et al. 2024 · a different site, after Carthage's fall

scenes.name: 8c New excavations
scenes.text: Since 2014, Tunisian-led excavations have been re-dating the precinct.
scenes.label: fact

scenes.name: 9a Shows / cannot show
left: Six centuries of infant and animal cremations
Careful burial, beneath stones carved with vows
An ancient accusation, made by outsiders
right: Whether all, some or none were sacrificed

scenes.name: 9b Uncertain as ever
scenes.text: "As uncertain as ever"
scenes.label: fact
scenes.sourceNote: Independent review · Bryn Mawr Classical Review, 2024

scenes.name: 10a Two stories
scenes.text: Offered to the gods, or mourned and buried with care?
scenes.label: open-question

scenes.name: 10b The ground
scenes.heading: The answer may still be in the ground beneath Carthage.
